holidays.name: National Paper Airplane Day
holidays.description: A day to fold, fling, and fly paper airplanes. Dust off your origami skills and see whose creation soars the farthest, or crashes most spectacularly into a coworker's coffee.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew out of aviation enthusiasts and paper-folding fans. It is often observed on May 26 in the United States and has spread through social media.
holidays.funFact: The world record for the longest paper airplane flight is over 88 meters (about 290 feet), set in 2012 by a team led by Joe Ayoob and John Collins, who used a custom-designed plane.

holidays.name: National Sugar Cookie Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the humble, buttery, sweet sugar cookie. Frost them, sprinkle them, cut them into shapes, or just eat them plain with a glass of milk.
holidays.origin: Observed in the U.S. as a food holiday on May 26 (some sources also list July 9). It celebrates a cookie traditionally linked to German settlers in Pennsylvania in the 1700s.
holidays.funFact: The sugar cookie is the official state cookie of Pennsylvania? Not quite, but the Nazareth, Pennsylvania Moravian sugar cake is a close ancestor, and the Moravian settlers' 'Nazareth sugar cookie' was actually named the official cookie of Pennsylvania in 2001.

holidays.name: World Dracula Day
holidays.description: A day for vampire fans to honor Bram Stoker's gothic classic with capes, fake fangs, garlic bread, and spooky readings of the novel.
holidays.origin: Celebrated on May 26 because Dracula was first published on May 26, 1897 by Archibald Constable and Company in London. The day was popularized in the 2010s by Dracula fans and Stoker's descendants.
holidays.funFact: Bram Stoker originally considered naming his vampire 'Count Wampyr' before finding the name Dracula in a book about Wallachia, and the novel was not an immediate bestseller.

holidays.name: Sally Ride Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the first American woman in space, inspiring kids and adults to look up, study science, and reach for the stars.
holidays.origin: Honors astronaut Sally Ride, who broke barriers aboard the Space Shuttle Challenger in 1983. The observance has been recognized in various forms to promote STEM education for girls.
holidays.funFact: Sally Ride was also a nationally ranked junior tennis player, and she is the youngest American to have traveled to space, at age 32.

holidays.name: Lost Sock Memorial Day
holidays.description: A mock-solemn day to remember all the socks that disappeared into the mysterious void of the laundry room. Bring your lonely single socks and give them a proper tribute.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, tongue-in-cheek observance said to be tied to the fact that socks mysteriously vanish in washers and dryers. It is commonly listed on May 9, but is also celebrated by many sock fans in late spring, including around this date.
holidays.funFact: Surveys have suggested the average person loses about 1.3 socks per month, adding up to about 15 lost socks every year.
